title: The end-to-end suite proves a killed CI job leaves nothing behind and a snapshot serves another host

story.as_a: factory release about to roll out
story.i_want_to: run the sandbox repo's CI through a killed job, an unreachable snapshot store and a hop between hosts
story.so_that: a regression back to shared CI state fails the suite before it reaches the fleet

rationale: PRD R7 assigns no end-to-end path to R8 by name, but the defect R8 exists for was found only in production: a killed job's Mix build lock hung later jobs on the same host for 600 s (chg#119, fixed in chg by 7bbc5dc with per-run roots and a per-job TMPDIR). US-52.58's guards check the workflow's text; only a real run on real fleet-ci hosts shows that nothing survives a job, that a missing snapshot store costs speed and not a red run, and that a snapshot built on one host is exact on another. The sandbox repo of the end-to-end suite is where such runs cost nothing.

acceptance_criteria.description: The suite installs into the sandbox repo a workflow rendered from e2e/sandbox/ci.yml.eex, whose test job uses the same container image digest, TMPDIR, MIX_TEST_PARTITION pattern, warm step and always-drop step as loopctl's Test job, and takes a workflow_dispatch input `host` that it adds to runs-on as `[self-hosted, fleet-ci, <host>]`.

Path ci_killed_job: the suite dispatches a sandbox run on host H, cancels it through the GitHub API once its compile step is in progress, dispatches a second run of the same commit on H, and passes only when the second run succeeds with its compile step under 120 s.
Path ci_snapshot_unreachable: a run dispatched with the input `snapshot_url` set to http://127.0.0.1:9 logs `snapshot: miss` from the warm step and still succeeds.

Path ci_cross_host_snapshot: after the sandbox's snapshot job publishes from host A, a run of the same commit on host B logs a snapshot hit with behind 0 and no `Compiling` line for the sandbox's own modules.

The sandbox workflow's last step, run if: always(), prints `leftover: <n>`, the number of databases on the CI Postgres whose name contains `_ci_<run_id>_`, after the drop; every path fails when a run it started logs a leftover above 0.

The three paths are tagged :ci_isolation, run with the rest of `mix e2e` nightly and on every factory release, and each fails, naming the run URL and the step, when a run it waits on has not finished within 30 minutes.

test_cases.name: the sandbox template matches loopctl's Test job (unit, no network)
preconditions: e2e/sandbox/ci.yml.eex rendered with host beelink; .github/workflows/ci.yml parsed
steps: compare container.image, env.TMPDIR, env.MIX_TEST_PARTITION's shape, the warm step's run text and the drop step
expected_results: equal on each; runs-on is [self-hosted, fleet-ci, beelink]

test_cases.name: e2e path ci_killed_job against mkreyman/loopctl-e2e-sandbox
preconditions: the sandbox repo with the rendered workflow pushed; a GitHub token able to dispatch and cancel its runs; host beelink
steps: dispatch run 1 on beelink; poll its jobs until the compile step is in_progress; cancel it
dispatch run 2 on beelink; wait for it
expected_results: run 2 succeeds; its compile step's duration < 120 s; both runs' logs (run 1's if: always() step included) show leftover: 0

test_cases.name: e2e path ci_snapshot_unreachable
expected_results: the warm step logs snapshot: miss; the run succeeds

test_cases.name: e2e path ci_cross_host_snapshot
preconditions: a sandbox commit pushed to master; hosts beelink (A) and x1 (B)
steps: wait for the master run's snapshot job on beelink to succeed
dispatch the same commit on x1; read the warm and compile step logs
expected_results: behind 0; no Compiling line for project modules

test_cases.name: a run that never finishes fails its path with the URL (unit, GitHub API stubbed)
preconditions: the suite's run-waiter with a stub API that always answers in_progress and an injected clock
steps: wait on a run with the clock advancing 31 minutes
expected_results: the path fails; the message carries the run URL and the in-progress step's name

technical_notes: The suite, its `mix e2e` task and the sandbox repo mkreyman/loopctl-e2e-sandbox are provided by release 2 (README names table: end-to-end suite). This story adds the paths under e2e/ and the template e2e/sandbox/ci.yml.eex; it adds no production code.
Template source of truth: loopctl's Test job as US-52.58 leaves it (.github/workflows/ci.yml:304 today). TC-52.59.1 is the guard that keeps the two from drifting.

Host labels: the fleet-ci pool registers each slot with its host's name as a label (infra runbooks/ci-runner-setup.md:42 for beelink's; per-host blocks at :1861-1945). ryzen is CI only while its model is off (infra decisions/0022), so the paths use beelink and x1 by default.

Cancelling: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/cancel; the compile step's state comes from GET .../runs/{run_id}/jobs. A cancelled job still runs its if: always() steps, so run 1's leftover line is readable.

The original defect and fix: chg adapters/elixir/test/integration_test.exs:12-19 (per-run roots named by OS pid and random bytes) and :59-60 (stale roots swept), chg .github/workflows/ci.yml:151-155 (per-job TMPDIR).
The CI Postgres and its reaper: infra runbooks/ci-runner-setup.md:800-869 (port 5433, `_ci_` names, reaper as backstop).
non_goals: The paths PRD R7 names for other releases (escalation, red CI, moves, messaging): their own releases.
Measuring CI wall clock: US-52.58's definition of done.
Any change to the workflow or to chg: US-52.58 and US-52.57.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.59.3: the suite cuts the job off from loopctl and the snapshot store and asserts the job still passes cold.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.59.5: each run reports the databases left behind for its run id, and any leftover fails the path, so per-job state is shown destroyed rather than assumed.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.59.2: a second run of the same commit after a killed one is the retry, and it must pass without waiting on anything the first left.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.59.6: every wait on a GitHub run is bounded at 30 minutes and fails with the run URL, so a stuck runner never hangs the nightly suite.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.59.4: the snapshot built on one host is consumed on another, through loopctl and the object store, never through the host's local disk.

definition_of_done: `mix e2e --only ci_isolation` passes from minis against the sandbox, and its output links the five runs it started.
With US-52.58's TMPDIR line removed from the sandbox template, ci_killed_job fails (checked once on a scratch branch, not committed).
defaults: Hosts: beelink as A and H, x1 as B (owner may change).
Compile budget after a killed run: 120 s; wait bound per run: 30 minutes.
